traceability.notes:
docs/stories/008.0-DEV-AUTO-FIX.story.md describes a focused iteration that adds ESLint auto-fix capabilities for two specific areas: (1) inserting placeholder @story annotations on functions/methods when missing, and (2) normalizing simple @story path suffix issues. The implementation:
- Enables `fixable: "code"` on traceability/require-story-annotation and wires in visitors/helpers that insert a single-line JSDoc `@story` comment immediately above the affected function/method/TS declaration, without touching runtime code or surrounding formatting. This is covered by tests in tests/rules/auto-fix-behavior-008.test.ts and aligns with REQ-AUTOFIX-MISSING, REQ-AUTOFIX-SAFE, and REQ-AUTOFIX-PRESERVE. - Enables `fixable: "code"` on traceability/valid-annotation-format but explicitly restricts fixes to @story path suffix normalization (adding `.md` to `.story` or `.story.md` when no extension exists), leaving all other text and whitespace unchanged. This matches REQ-AUTOFIX-FORMAT, REQ-AUTOFIX-SAFE, REQ-AUTOFIX-PRESERVE, and the error-handling acceptance criterion by not attempting fixes in ambiguous cases. - Provides user-facing documentation in user-docs/api-reference.md that explains what `--fix` does for each rule and clearly states the safety constraints and current limitations, satisfying the Documentation acceptance criterion. - Has comprehensive tests (including tests/rules/auto-fix-behavior-008.test.ts and the broader valid-annotation-format tests) that all pass under `npm test -- --verbose`, demonstrating correct behavior and integration with the ESLint toolchain.
The story itself marks REQ-AUTOFIX-TEMPLATE and REQ-AUTOFIX-SELECTIVE as "Not yet implemented" and positions them as future enhancements, not part of the current acceptance criteria. Given that all in-scope acceptance criteria and implemented requirements (REQ-AUTOFIX-MISSING, REQ-AUTOFIX-FORMAT, REQ-AUTOFIX-SAFE, REQ-AUTOFIX-PRESERVE) are demonstrably satisfied by code, tests, and documentation, this story is assessed as PASSED for its defined scope.
